tier1.text: Each ulnar artery carries blood to the forearm, wrist and hand. This artery begins where the brachial artery, the artery of the upper arm, splits into the radial and ulnar arteries. The ulnar artery runs along the ulna, the forearm bone on the pinky-finger side. At the wrist, the ulnar artery joins the radial artery to form the palmar arches, which supply blood to the hand.

quotes.quote: As the brachial artery approaches the coronoid fossa, it bifurcates into the radial and ulnar arteries, which continue into the forearm, or antebrachium.

quotes.quote: The radial artery and ulnar artery parallel their namesake bones, giving off smaller branches until they reach the wrist, or carpal region. At this level, they fuse to form the superficial and deep palmar arches that supply blood to the hand
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: palmar arches: superficial and deep arches formed from anastomoses of the radial and ulnar arteries; supply blood to the hand and digital arteries
